title: Nippard shrugs (wide grip/snatch grip shrugs) tutorial
summary: NH demonstrates his snatch-grip strapped shrug variation (idea from Jeff Nippard) that emphasises a loaded forward stretch of the whole upper back rather than the top squeeze. He covers setup, knee break to limit thoracic rounding, biceps risk from the snatch grip, and his scheme of 4 sets of 12-15 with evolving rep ranges, showing it with 300 lb.

claims.claim: This snatch-grip stretch shrug targets the whole yoke: upper traps, rear delts and mid traps.
Use straps for snatch-grip shrugs even with a strong hook grip, since you go for reps; without straps it becomes a different lift.
A normal snatch-grip shrug mainly works the upper traps; he wants a more global upper-back stimulus.
Let the shoulders protract forward so the traps catch the bar in a stretch, then squeeze back rather than up; focus on the stretch, not the top contraction.
He does strict squeeze-focused shrugs after every pull session as part of a neck/yoke overload protocol, so these stretch shrugs are for heavy loaded stretch instead.
Weighted stretch is extremely efficient for muscles that can take it without injury risk; trap tear risk here is practically nil.
Shoulders could be at risk from the forward stretch, but he never felt discomfort because the upper back catches the weight.
The snatch grip stretches the biceps at an unusual angle; if you don't otherwise train snatch-grip, consider skipping this lift or start very light, since arms act as ropes that can snap.
He uses snatch grips in many lifts, so by the principle of specificity his body is adapted to this one.
Never do these with a supinated grip.
Pick the bar up with a leg-driven partial pull, not your lower back; bend the knees.
Breaking at the knee lets the whole upper back stretch while limiting thoracic rounding; a little rounding is OK but mitigate it.
He shows the lift with 300 lb, though his working weight is four plates.
The movement should be safe on the lower back and legs since it starts from a partial pull; stop if you feel lower back pain.
On the last rep, let the bar stretch a bit longer in the back position.
You'll feel strong upper and mid trap involvement; any discomfort he felt was in the middle of the upper back.
He keeps these at 12-15 reps, 4 sets with evolving rep ranges, using intensity as a risk-reward tool to protect his arms; high reps give a pump and let him feel a risky extra rep coming.

exercises.name: Snatch-grip stretch shrug (Nippard shrug)
cues: pick up with legs, partial pull
let shoulders protract and stretch forward
break at the knee to limit thoracic rounding
pause in stretch on last rep
exercises.why: loaded stretch overloads the whole yoke (upper/mid traps, rear delts)
